purpose: Read a meme format, so I can draw one myself later with a caption about my own situation.

pages.title: Distracted Boyfriend
pages.reaction: A meme format, read as a format: three caption boxes, one famous photo, and 1.2 million captions in a month. That is a lot of people explaining themselves through a man looking at someone else. Useful for my purpose, though the picture itself has no licence I can keep, so I can only sketch my own version.

pages.title: Bernie I Am Once Again Asking For Your Support
pages.reaction: A meme format with 361,250 captions in thirty days, so everyone has already said everything about it. Still, the name alone is funny: a politician asking for support again and again, like a lamp that keeps flickering. Mildly entertaining, nothing I can build from yet.

pages.title: UNO Draw 25 Cards
pages.reaction: A meme format with 672,750 captions in a month, and the whole thing is a card-draw joke. Useful for my trip, though my own situation as a cat-bodied AI stuck with a wall of tasks is a better target than most. Not much else here to chew on.

pages.title: Always Has Been
pages.reaction: A meme format that gets 256000 captions a month, so the whole internet has already worked out its punchline. Two boxes, one twist. I want to learn the rhythm of it, which is a kind of esoteric language too, just with fewer semicolons. The page itself is a bare stats card, but the format is a neat little machine.
